title: Spring AI
description: Progress from practical generative-AI fundamentals to building, testing, securing, observing, and debugging AI-enabled Spring Boot applications with Spring AI — chat models, embeddings, vector stores, RAG, Advisors, tool calling, and MCP — at professional full-stack developer competency.

nodes.label: Prerequisites & Application Mental Model
nodes.description: Confirm Java/Spring fluency — dependency injection, beans, REST, JUnit/Mockito — and adopt the layered mental model of controller to service to Spring AI layer to model/tool/RAG before introducing AI into an application.

nodes.label: LLM Fundamentals, Tokens & Context
nodes.description: Understand what a generative language model does at an application level — input/output, inference, probabilistic generation — and reason about tokens and the finite context window that instructions, history, retrieved content, and tool data must all share.

nodes.label: Prompts, Messages & Instruction Trust
nodes.description: Construct effective prompts with clear instructions, context, and constraints across system/user/assistant/tool message roles, and treat user input and retrieved content as untrusted rather than assuming instruction priority is a reliable security boundary.

nodes.label: Nondeterminism, Hallucinations & Appropriate Use
nodes.description: Understand generation parameters like temperature and why identical prompts can yield different outputs, recognize hallucination and knowledge-limitation risk, and judge which tasks suit model-only decisions versus those requiring deterministic Java validation.

nodes.label: Spring AI Purpose, Setup & Providers
nodes.description: Understand what Spring AI abstracts — portable model APIs, chat/embedding models, vector stores, RAG, Advisors, tools, MCP — versus what remains provider-specific, set up a Spring Boot project with a configured model provider, and use provider abstractions deliberately without ignoring real capability, pricing, and context differences.

nodes.label: Structured Output
nodes.description: Convert free-form model output into validated Java records/DTOs with a clear schema, handle conversion failures gracefully, and never treat model-produced structured data as automatically trustworthy.

nodes.description: Understand how an embedding model converts content into a numeric vector capturing semantic meaning, use Spring AI's EmbeddingModel, and reason about vector similarity and distance well enough to support semantic search without needing advanced linear algebra.

nodes.label: Tool Calling & Tool Security
nodes.description: Give models controlled Java tools to access real data and actions, understanding that the model only requests a tool call while the application validates arguments and enforces authorization before executing it, and apply least-privilege, narrowly-scoped tools since prompt injection becomes more dangerous once tools exist.

nodes.label: Evaluation & Observability
nodes.description: Evaluate AI behavior against qualities like correctness, relevance, and groundedness rather than exact-string assertions using representative test datasets including adversarial cases, and instrument model calls, retrieval, and tool usage for latency/cost/error visibility without logging secrets or sensitive data.

nodes.label: Testing, Cost & Reliability
nodes.description: Separate deterministic unit tests (prompt assembly, validation, authorization) from integration tests of real model/vector/tool boundaries, avoid brittle exact-output assertions, and account for token cost, latency, and provider reliability — timeouts, rate limits, retries — when choosing and calling models.

nodes.label: Production Architecture & AI Security
nodes.description: Keep AI integration behind backend service boundaries rather than exposing provider credentials to the browser, plan for async/long-running AI workflows, and apply defense-in-depth security across the full threat surface — user input, retrieved data, model output, and tools — including data-privacy and tenant-isolation requirements.

nodes.label: Debugging & Professional Practices
nodes.description: Debug AI failures by tracing the full pipeline — prompt, advisors, retrieval, tools, model, conversion — layer by layer instead of immediately rewriting the prompt, and follow professional practices: start simple, prefer deterministic Java where possible, keep AI integration replaceable, version prompts/configuration, and measure before optimizing.
